questions.q: What must the body of an inline table-valued function (iTVF) be?
options: A WHILE loop that builds rows one at a time
A BEGIN/END block with multiple statements
A stored procedure call
A single SELECT statement, with no BEGIN/END
questions.explain: An iTVF is declared RETURNS TABLE AS RETURN (SELECT ...) — the entire body is one SELECT, wrapped in parentheses after RETURN.

questions.q: How do you call an iTVF in a query?
options: In the SELECT list, like a scalar expression
With the CALL statement
In a FROM clause, like a table, optionally passing it parameters
Only from inside another function
questions.explain: Because an iTVF returns rows, you call it in FROM — SELECT * FROM dbo.FnName(@value) — not in the SELECT list.

questions.q: Why doesn't an iTVF have the scalar UDF's row-by-row performance problem?
options: Because its single SELECT can be substituted directly into the calling query and optimized as one combined plan
Because iTVFs always run on a background thread
Because iTVFs cache their results permanently the first time they run
Because iTVFs are not allowed to accept parameters
questions.explain: Since the iTVF's body is literally one SELECT, the optimizer can expand it in place, the same way it handles a parameterized view — no black-box per-row call is involved.

questions.q: What's the closest mental model for an iTVF?
options: A trigger that fires on SELECT
A parameterized view — a saved SELECT you can query like a table, with an argument
A stored procedure that returns no results
A scalar UDF with a table-typed parameter
questions.explain: An iTVF is essentially a view with a parameter slot — the optimizer can see through it the same way it sees through a view.

questions.q: Which of these is a correctly shaped iTVF declaration?
options: CREATE FUNCTION dbo.FnName(@id int) RETURNS int AS RETURN (SELECT * FROM T WHERE Id = @id);
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.FnName(@id int) RETURNS TABLE AS BEGIN SELECT * FROM T WHERE Id = @id; END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.FnName(@id int) RETURNS TABLE AS RETURN (SELECT * FROM T WHERE Id = @id);
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.FnName(@id int) RETURNS TABLE AS RETURN (SELECT * FROM T WHERE Id = @id);
questions.explain: RETURNS TABLE paired with AS RETURN (single SELECT) — no BEGIN/END — is the defining shape of an inline table-valued function.
